plan.title: Paired treatment DE in blood, subject-blocked DESeq2 + ORA
plan.analytical_narrative: Ten blood RNA-seq samples (STAR/featureCounts gene counts, 12,000 genes) from 5 subjects, each contributing a control and a treated sample. The paired structure is the central feature of this design: within-subject variability (genetic background, baseline immune state) dwarfs between-subject variability, so a naive two-group test that ignores pairing would waste most of its power and could even be confounded by subject-to-subject differences unrelated to treatment. The plan therefore blocks on subject throughout. Step 1 profiles sample structure (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to confirm the 5 paired subjects separate primarily by subject and that no sample is a mislabeled outlier before any test is fit. Step 2 fits DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition (condition releveled so 'control' is the reference), which estimates the treatment effect within each subject and removes it from the between-subject noise; apeglm shrinkage is applied to the condition coefficient, BH-adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering select the responding genes, and the count-outlier / NA-p-value policy of DESeq2 (n=5 per cell, below the 7-replicate switch to replacement) is reported explicitly. Step 3 takes the resulting gene list — genes with a treatment effect within each subject — and asks what biological processes and pathways it converges on, using over-representation analysis with an explicit tested-gene universe (required by policy over a preranked GSEA for this discrete-list question) against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human collections, plus a GO-BP scan reduced with rrvgo to representative terms; if the significant list falls under ~50 genes, the report states so and treats the ORA result as exploratory. Step 4 assembles the full report: design, contrast direction, thresholds, diagnostic plots, DE gene table with shrunken and unshrunken log2FC, and the enrichment results with their reference-collection versions and caveats.
